question: Should OpenClaw core support native cross-gateway session messaging now, and should the concrete path be the narrow gateway-peers session-tool PR or a broader federation/session-resume contract first?
rationale: The request would create a new cross-gateway trust and session ownership boundary, so maintainers need to choose the supported API and security model before implementation.

options.title: Design federation first
options.body: Keep this issue as the concrete tracker while maintainers define identity, authorization, transcript ownership, and delivery semantics before merging code.

options.title: Advance linked PR
options.body: Use the open gateway-peers PR as the implementation path after resolving conflicts, proof, and security review.

options.title: Defer core support
options.body: Document plugin, MCP, channel, or SSH-style workarounds and close only if maintainers reject native core routing.

recommendation.title: Design federation first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the concrete tracker while maintainers define identity, authorization, transcript ownership, and delivery semantics before merging code.

likelyOwner.reason: The session-tool and gateway URL security history is the strongest available ownership signal for the product/security choice.
